summary: Washburn County, Wisconsin fire tower listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; the sources read give no build date, design or history.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone; no source read describes what, if anything, remains at the site.

evidence.supports: listed as Tower Gone at 45.81071, -91.64763 in Washburn County
statewide network mostly in forested and fire-prone regions
evidence.quote: Wisconsin once had a vast fire tower lookout network, mostly in the forested and most fire prone regions of the state.
At the height of their use, 119 towers dotted the landscape.

evidence.supports: topographic-map site index for Washburn County carries the name Potato Lake Fire Tower

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The only tower-specific source is the Forest Fire Lookout Association list (name, coordinates, Tower Gone, no register number). No build date, design, height, staffing, fires or description of the current site was found in the two web searches, the cached pages, or the pages read. The TopoZone name is a map-index entry, not evidence that a tower stood or stands there. The story is short on purpose: it is below the usual 120-word floor because there is nothing honest to add. Re-check with the Washburn County Historical Society or DNR fire-tower records if a fuller story is wanted.
